index.md:
VibeScroll connects saved posts, cited insights and private project plans across the website and your assistant. Start with the result you want. Each workflow identifies its tools, waiting points and funding boundary.

## Choose a workflow

- [Find and save a post](/docs/workflows/find-save): search existing knowledge or save one supplied link.
- [Get insights and track progress](/docs/workflows/analyze): reuse ready results or choose a supported analysis route.
- [Compare and select analysis versions](/docs/workflows/reanalyze): preserve an existing result while requesting or reviewing another version.
- [Apply insights to a project](/docs/workflows/proposals): use the full post context and save a chat-written proposal.
- [Discuss and revise a plan](/docs/workflows/discussion): resume discussion across chats or choose quoted API generation.
- [Approve an issue and follow the work](/docs/workflows/handoff): publish one reviewed issue and distinguish reports from observed outcomes.

## Understand the connection

- [How the MCP works](/docs/mcp): what makes a model choose a tool, how requests reach Convex, and what the server can see.
- [Subscriptions and authentication](/docs/mcp/subscription): use your host's model allowance for in-chat work; distinguish VibeScroll OAuth, processing credits and API funding.
- [Use saved insights in a chat](/docs/mcp/first-workflow): a first read-and-plan workflow without a paid model job.

## Look up the contract

- [Tool reference](/docs/mcp/tools): actual names, descriptions, strict input schemas, OAuth scopes and side-effect hints, generated from the registry.
- [Results, limits and errors](/docs/mcp/results): output families, pagination, version binding, evidence and billing states.
- [Skills and Events](/docs/mcp/skills): the nine packaged skills and the separate background monitor.
- [Shared data and Convex usage](/docs/mcp/efficiency): current read shapes, known limits and proposed improvements.
- [Host support](/docs/mcp/host-support): website, custom MCP, skills, images and Events, with verification limits.
- [Contribute to the docs](/docs/contributing): source, generation and synthetic example checks.
- [Changelog](/docs/changelog): published checkpoints and the current local candidate.

## Verification and source

This documentation was audited against the November 1, 2026 implementation. Tool availability depends on deployed feature flags, permissions and what your host has discovered. Generated descriptors describe the full supported registry; they do not prove that every tool is visible in every connected chat.

The [MIT source](https://github.com/StefanDG1/vibescroll) includes the MCP registry, strict contracts, plugin skills and tests. Public documentation uses synthetic examples and does not query your library. The docs interface uses [Fumadocs](https://github.com/fuma-nama/fumadocs), an MIT-licensed React documentation framework.
first-workflow.md:
This walkthrough reads an existing analyzed post and saves a project plan written in the chat. It starts no paid analysis or implementation job.

## Connect once

1. Sign in to ChatGPT or Codex using the account and usage route you want.
2. Connect the existing VibeScroll plugin/MCP endpoint and complete VibeScroll OAuth. Follow [the connection guide](/connect) for the supported host setup.
3. Ask: “Use VibeScroll to list my available workspaces and saved insights. Do not start analysis or spend credits.” The assistant can use `get_profile` and `search`.

The same connection includes current joined team workspaces by default. Personal posts stay in the personal workspace until shared. Any workspace access explicitly turned off for that OAuth client stays off; joining a team does not override it. Team roles and each member's own Pro remain authoritative. No second setup is required for each team.

If the result requires a workspace selection, choose one of the returned workspaces. If it requires authentication, use the host's connection flow. A profile-selection error is not a reason to create another plugin.

## Read a post and a project

Ask: “Use the saved insights from this post to suggest a plan for my selected project. Read the current VibeScroll project context first. Write the plan here without starting an API plan job.”

The assistant can retrieve a chosen search result with `fetch`, then read `get_project_application_context` for the exact post/version and project. The context includes saved insights and a confirmed project profile. It does not contain inspected repository code. Grant separate repository access if you want code-specific verification.

Pagination fields matter: a short or empty page is not proof that the whole library has been searched. The assistant should follow the returned cursor when needed.

## Save and resume the plan

1. Discuss changes in the chat. This uses your host's model allowance.
2. Ask the assistant to save the agreed plan with `save_project_proposal`, using the exact returned context hash and version references. A first save uses `expectedVersion=0` and a stable operation key.
3. Open the returned VibeScroll review URL. The same saved proposal can be found later through `list_project_proposals` and `get_project_proposal`.

An edit must first read the current version/review and context. A stale version means reconcile the newer result, not overwrite it or start another proposal to hide the conflict.

## Publish only the reviewed issue

Ask to preview the exact GitHub issue with `preview_project_issue`. If you approve that proposal version and exact payload, the assistant can use `approve_project_issue` with the returned binding and operation key. GitHub authorization and repository access are separate requirements.

The tool publishes the approved issue; it does not automatically start Codex implementation. An unknown publication result must be reconciled, not blindly retried. A later `report_project_outcome` is an assistant report; signed GitHub observations and verified tests remain distinct evidence.
find-save.md:
Find a saved result first, or save the exact link you want to keep. A compatible ready result can be reused without another analysis charge.

## Find existing insights

1. Ask: "Search my VibeScroll library for deployment rollback ideas. Read only; do not start analysis."
2. Choose a returned workspace if more than one is available. Use `get_profile` for approved workspace IDs.
3. Use `search(mode="ranked_v1")` with a short query. Optional filters narrow category, platform and known direct-save dates. To search across teams explicitly, pass up to three returned `workspaceIds` and omit `profileId`. Each workspace needs current whole-workspace library access for ranked mode. A source/space-limited connection uses compatible search without `mode` and the ranked-only fields; it does not require broader permissions or another login. `projectId` adds explainable topic fit for the returned page. Prefer `next_cursor` for complete continuation, including matches beyond the first twenty. The older `next_offset` only moves between candidate-post pages. An empty filtered page does not establish whole-library absence.
4. Read selected results with `fetch`. Ranked post records provide a `fetch_id`; their `id` groups matches and is not a fetch locator. Keep the active profile and any exact sharing-grant/version references, citations and analysis version.

If a paraphrase misses useful candidates, the assistant can try up to two alternative short queries and merge canonical post/version references. This is bounded query expansion, not semantic vector search. Exact source references go directly to `fetch`.

The visible result is cited saved knowledge. Reading it starts no model generation on VibeScroll's servers. Your host can use its own allowance to explain the returned material.

## Use a particular post as a reference

Ask: "Read this post's retained transcript, screenshots and insights, then help me create something in its style. Do not analyze it again."

The assistant uses `fetch(format="post_context_v1")` for that exact post/version and follows its `context.next_cursor` for remaining context items. The response separates insights, transcript segments and observations by their original IDs. Its frame manifest lists each sampled screenshot once. `read_post_frame` returns actual native JPEG content when the agent needs to inspect an image. Read frames one at a time. Several insight citations can refer to the same frame.

Team results carry their exact sharing-grant reference and version, which subsequent reads preserve. Each request checks current access. No job, worker lease, acknowledgment or new analysis credits are created by these reads. Unavailable evidence is reported rather than downloaded again. Retained context can contain sampled frames and a retained transcript; it does not promise the original full video or complete visual coverage.

## Save a supplied link

Ask: "Save this link to VibeScroll without analysis." The assistant uses `save_link` with `analyze=false`, an inferred factual title and one stable request key. Keep the returned source ID and post URL.

For ordinary analysis requests, the reviewed connection defaults determine the supported automatic route. Save-only requests stay save-only. GitHub and Reddit links save metadata and use their own review path; they do not inherit video extraction authority. Other unsupported sources require an upload or supplied text in the website.

## Continue from the receipt

- If a compatible result is ready, open or fetch it. Reuse avoids another analysis, although data delivery still uses infrastructure.
- If the post is saved but empty, choose [analysis](/docs/workflows/analyze) only when you want insights.
- If it is queued, waiting or running, keep the same source and use bounded status checks or the configured monitor.
- If the reply is unknown, preserve the request key and reconcile the same save. Do not create replacement analysis.
- If access or a version binding changed, read current state before continuing. A workspace choice needs a returned workspace ID, not a new connection.

Metadata can appear before insights. A title, thumbnail or saved receipt is not completed analysis. Use [vibescroll-save](/docs/mcp/skills#vibescroll-save) for the packaged workflow and [host support](/docs/mcp/host-support) for availability.
analyze.md:
Get insights from a saved supported video while keeping its actual route, progress and credit state visible.

## Reuse or quote before starting

1. Read the exact source with `get_job_status` or `video_analysis_status`.
2. If compatible insights are ready, reuse them. Cache reuse starts no new analysis and remains zero-credit for that analysis.
3. If work is active or unknown, keep its run and version references. Do not start another job.
4. For a new prepared request, call `quote_video_analysis`. Review its route, maximum credits, model and evidence reuse before accepting it.
5. Start an accepted quote with `start_video_analysis`, keeping its exact quote hash, maximum, settings and one stable key.

The ordinary configured native flow can return a `request_analysis` next action. Follow that returned action with its exact source and profile. Do not replace it with a different executor or funding mode.

## Use the chosen funding route

Hosted API analysis uses the quoted VibeScroll credits and finite provider funding. A ChatGPT subscription does not fund a server API call merely because the request came from ChatGPT.

The prepared `work_cloud` route uses server preparation and a configured native task for analysis. Preparation may cost credits; the native reasoning uses that user's host allowance. The task reads retained evidence and actual JPEGs. An arbitrary active chat is not automatically that authorized task. Local execution remains deferred.

## Follow observed progress

Use `video_analysis_status` for preparation, analysis, validation and saved-result state. Open the returned post link to resume the same work on the website. A quote maximum or credit hold is not a final charge. A missing final amount is not proof of zero usage.

If the result is waiting or queued, use the configured Events task or a bounded follow-up. No progress percentage or completion time is guaranteed. If the monitor is absent or paused, fix that route's setup without treating it as an OAuth failure.

For a confirmed failure, use only the returned eligible recovery action. A stale quote requires a fresh quote. Cancelled unclaimed work and unknown dispatched work have different remedies. Unknown work retains its exposure until reconciled; it must not trigger an automatic paid fallback.

Once ready, read the saved version or [apply all its insights to a project](/docs/workflows/proposals). To request a deliberate second analysis, use [the version workflow](/docs/workflows/reanalyze).
reanalyze.md:
Compare another analysis without losing a valid saved result. A newer model name or higher reasoning setting does not establish better quality.

## Read the existing versions

1. Call `analysis_history` for the exact source.
2. Read a chosen version with `analysis_version`.
3. Compare two retained versions with `compare_analysis_versions`.

These reads generate no analysis. Keep immutable version IDs separate from the currently selected version and its selection revision. Explain differences using the evidence, rather than automatically promoting the newest result.

## Request a deliberate new version

For the prepared route, review `quote_video_analysis` with `reanalyze=true` and start only the exact accepted quote. Reusable retained evidence can avoid another download or transcription. The quote states what is actually reused and funded.

For a supported native retained-evidence request, use `request_analysis_version` with the current selection revision and a stable key. Keep its attempt ID throughout the worker lease. The worker must inspect actual retained JPEGs before completion. This route grants no new downloader, ASR or paid API authority.

The incumbent remains available while the candidate is waiting or running. If the start reply is unknown, reconcile the existing attempt. A confirmed failure does not erase the good version or justify switching funding.

## Select or cancel explicitly

Use `select_analysis_version` only when the user chooses that retained version, including a rollback. Pass the current selection revision. Selection starts no analysis and spends no credits.

If the selection revision is stale, read history and reconcile the choice. To cancel an explicitly selected, still-unclaimed native attempt, use `cancel_waiting_analysis_version`. It cannot reset a running or unknown task. Preserve its result and funding records until the actual state is known.

Ready-cache reuse remains distinct from reanalysis. Choosing a new requested model does not relabel a cached output's original provenance. Continue with [project context](/docs/workflows/proposals) using the exact version you intend.
proposals.md:
Turn a saved post's insights into a private project proposal, then resume that same proposal from another chat or the website.

## Read the full post context

1. Find the intended project through `get_profile` and read the saved analysis.
2. Call `get_project_application_context` with the exact source, project and intended analysis version.
3. Use all returned post insights by default, up to twenty. Pass a narrower insight selection only when the user requests it.
4. Keep its context hash, version, insight IDs and repository references for the save.

A project profile is not inspected repository code. Inspect separately authorized code before making code-specific implementation claims. Keep no-fit, already implemented, unsupported, needs-context and deferred judgments visible.

If analysis is still pending, follow the existing [analysis state](/docs/workflows/analyze). A ready shared result needs no repeated model job. If project access or retained evidence is unavailable, resolve that exact limitation before saving a claimed evidence-backed plan.

## Write in chat and save

Ask: "Discuss a plan here using this post's full insights. Save the agreed proposal without starting an API generation job."

Use your host's reasoning to write the proposal. Persist it with `save_project_proposal`, using `expectedVersion=0` for creation and one stable key. The server supplies citations. Saving supplied text starts no paid generation, issue publication or coding.

The visible result is a durable proposal ID and review URL. `draft_project_suggestion` remains a separate route for an exact existing server evaluation; do not invent evaluation IDs for a chat-written plan.

## Resume and revise

Find the proposal with `list_project_proposals`, following its cursor even across empty filtered pages. Open the selected ID with `get_project_proposal`.

Before editing, read its current version, review state and context. Keep the source, project, analysis and insight binding. Save with the current expected version and review plus a new key for that intentional edit. If the response is unknown, retry identical content with the same key. If it is stale, reconcile the newer record before saving.

Use [discussion](/docs/workflows/discussion) to keep feedback with the proposal. A saved draft remains separate from [Approve & create issue](/docs/workflows/handoff).
discussion.md:
Keep plan feedback and revisions attached to one saved proposal. Another chat can read the same discussion without recreating the draft.

## Read and persist discussion

1. Call `get_proposal_discussion` for the saved proposal.
2. Follow `continueCursor` when older messages are needed.
3. Discuss the plan in the active chat using the full retained post context.
4. Save requested feedback or a chat-written response with `add_proposal_message`, the current version and a stable key.

This persistence call generates no model answer on VibeScroll's servers. The host's model allowance covers the conversation. Save an agreed plan revision through `save_project_proposal` using its current binding.

If an edit is stale, reread and reconcile intervening feedback. If an acknowledgement is unknown, keep the same key and identical text. Neither state calls for a duplicate proposal. Missing access or evidence needs its specific recovery, rather than paid generation.

## Choose hosted generation explicitly

If you want VibeScroll to generate the plan, call `quote_project_plan`. Review its exact version, quote ID and maximum credits. The quote itself reserves nothing.

Use `start_project_plan` for the accepted generation quote. Use `reply_to_project_plan` when the user chooses a quoted reply that saves their message and queues a refinement atomically. Ordinary `add_proposal_message` remains the persistence route without paid generation.

Read `get_proposal_discussion` to distinguish queued, running, ready, failed and unknown operations. Insufficient user credits and unavailable provider capacity are different blockers. Preserve unknown exposure and do not switch funding or start replacement work. A changed quote needs a new review.

A ready plan can still need project context or revision. Completed generation is not issue approval. Existing insights remain reusable without another video analysis. When the exact plan is ready for publication, continue with [the issue handoff](/docs/workflows/handoff).
handoff.md:
Use one **Approve & create issue** action for the exact saved plan. Then follow the same work record without treating issue creation as implementation.

## Preview and approve one issue

1. Read the current proposal and discussion. If generation is pending or unknown, reconcile it before choosing a plan to publish.
2. Call `preview_project_issue` to check the repository, visibility, current version and context hash.
3. Show the exact plan and publication destination to the user.
4. After the user's explicit approval of that plan and issue creation, call `approve_project_issue` with the returned binding, acknowledgement and a stable key.
5. Read `get_proposal_discussion` for confirmed publication and the issue link.

Preview starts no publication. Approval queues the frozen issue operation and starts no coding or model generation. GitHub access is separate from VibeScroll OAuth. A stale plan needs another read and review; an old approval cannot authorize a changed payload.

`prepare_project_issue` supports a private frozen handoff for an independently authorized publishing integration. It prepares text and completion instructions without publishing. Prefer the combined approval path for the normal workflow.

## Recover the existing publication

If publication is queued, keep its operation ID. If GitHub setup fails, repair that setup and use `retry_project_issue` for the same saved operation. If dispatch is ambiguous, reconcile by authoritative lookup. Do not create a replacement issue or send a second publication after dispatch.

Open the confirmed issue or copy its work prompt to the intended assistant. Coding, spending, merging and deployment still depend on the user's actual implementation instructions. Existing post insights are reused; issue creation needs no repeated video analysis.

## Report and inspect outcomes

An implementing assistant can call `report_project_outcome` through its authenticated connection for the exact handoff. Include an honest completed, blocked or failed status, actual same-repository work links, and the actual commit or null. Keep the same report key and content after an unknown reply.

Signed GitHub observations and authenticated assistant reports remain separate evidence. Issue state is bound to the confirmed publication. A PR can associate itself by including that issue's exact proposal locator and handoff marker plus a same-repository closing reference. Signed observations retain its head/merge commit and individual check facts. The implementing assistant should preserve these public identifiers from the issue instructions; they grant no callback access. Full PR/check acceptance still depends on the App's enabled events and actual deliveries. An individual successful check is not proof all CI passed. Issue closure, a model report or a merged PR alone does not establish measured benefit.

Use `record_feedback` for the user's explicit judgment about current source evidence. A judgment or reported outcome does not silently alter the plan's review or authorize further work. See [host support and verification](/docs/mcp/host-support).
tools.md:
The reference groups tools by the action you want to perform. Filters connect workflows, packaged skills, effects and funding. Search and the alphabetical index preserve direct lookup. Existing tool names and permanent anchors remain unchanged.

The descriptors come from `packages/mcp/server.ts` through a synthetic `tools/list` request. That request executes no tool and uses no real account. Group, skill and workflow labels come from `packages/mcp/tool-guide.ts`. The runtime remains the authority for schemas, scopes and annotations.

## Availability and versioning

The reference includes feature-gated native execution and compact UI tools. A particular host may expose a subset because of deployment flags, scopes, host support or cached metadata. Events subscription methods are separate from ordinary `tools/call` tools. Repository source alone does not prove the current connected host discovered a new tool.

The server validates inputs with strict schemas. Most outputs currently have no published per-tool `outputSchema`; the [result reference](/docs/mcp/results) explains their actual families and meanings. Input schema validation is not an output-completeness guarantee.

## Tool families and effects

| Family                                          | Purpose                                                         | AI or external effects                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_profile`, `search`, `fetch`                | Discover authorized workspaces and retrieve saved knowledge     | No model generation                                                       |
| Project context and proposal reads              | Read exact insight/project context, plans and discussions       | No model generation                                                       |
| `save_project_proposal`, `add_proposal_message` | Persist text written by the chat                                | Writes data, no model generation                                          |
| Video/plan quote and start                      | Estimate or begin explicitly funded work                        | Quote does not start generation; start can reserve credits and queue work |
| Issue preview/approve/retry                     | Freeze and publish the reviewed issue                           | Approval can write to GitHub; unknown state requires reconciliation       |
| Feedback/outcome reports                        | Store a supplied judgment or report                             | No proof of implementation or business outcome                            |
| Version history/selection/reanalysis            | Read immutable results or deliberately select/request a version | Reanalysis can start funded work; selection preserves history             |
| `work_cloud_*`                                  | Exact leased native job and prepared evidence exchange          | Restricted worker authority; not general library access                   |
| Compact UI tools                                | Open or update the supported embedded view                      | Availability depends on host UI support                                   |

## Generated descriptors

Each tool below has a permanent anchor. `readOnlyHint` describes the requested operation, not all transport overhead: even a library read currently performs authenticated throttling. `idempotentHint` is a client hint; writes still require their exact version/idempotency bindings. OAuth scopes are necessary but current membership, grants and funding checks remain authoritative.

The funding label **No AI generation** describes the tool's model behavior. It does not mean that authentication, database reads, storage or external services have no infrastructure cost. **Quote** reserves nothing. A start tool still requires the exact returned quote and current authority. See [funding routes](/docs/mcp/subscription) before choosing one.
results.md:
Ordinary successful calls return a JSON value in both MCP text `content` and `structuredContent`. These represent the same result, not two jobs. The compact UI may use additional routing metadata. A retained-frame call instead returns metadata text and a native JPEG image attachment.

## What each read returns

| Tool                              | Data returned                                                                                         | Current bound or exclusion                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_profile({})`                 | Authorized workspace/grant metadata and coverage                                                      | 10 profile records examined per page                                                                                                                       |
| `get_profile({profileId})`        | Selected workspace, granted project profiles and current evaluation summaries                         | Up to 5 full project profiles and 5 evaluations per project; no repository files or general chat history                                                   |
| `search`, legacy                  | Matching insight IDs, titles, URLs, excerpts and coverage                                             | Examines 5 permitted posts per page; at most 20 matches; title 200 characters, excerpt 600                                                                 |
| `search(mode="ranked_v1")`        | Compact post records and referring post/insight matches in the active workspace                       | At most 50 indexed candidates and 4 source hydrations per call, 20 matches, 200 candidates per signed continuation session; current-index coverage can lag |
| `fetch`, legacy/structured        | Selected insight or saved analysis text and citation summaries                                        | First 20 insights, claims up to 2,000 characters, up to 10 evidence summaries per insight; no raw transcript/media                                         |
| `fetch(format="post_context_v1")` | Exact retained post/version, metadata, insights, transcript segments, observations and frame manifest | Bounded pages below100,000 UTF-8 bytes; follow context.next_cursor; frames are sampled and contain no image bytes in this manifest                         |
| `read_post_frame`                 | One actual native JPEG plus exact frame/version/evidence metadata                                     | At most150,000 decoded bytes; verifies size/hash/dimensions and current authority before and after storage I/O; no worker acknowledgment                   |
| `get_project_application_context` | Version/hash references, saved summary, post insights, confirmed project profile and prior proposals  | At most 20 selected insights; 120,000 bytes of context data before the context hash and MCP envelope; no repository code or raw media                      |
| `list_project_proposals`          | Titles, IDs, versions and dispositions                                                                | 10 examined proposals per page; project filtering can leave an empty page with a cursor                                                                    |
| `get_proposal_discussion`         | Current plan/context, discussion, latest operations and issue state                                   | 20 non-tool discussion messages per page                                                                                                                   |
| `video_analysis_status`           | Executor, stages, quote/charge/billing, failure, catalog/version/post links                           | Last 20 stages; no private logs or raw provider response                                                                                                   |
| `analysis_version`                | Saved output, model provenance and version/evidence hashes                                            | Assistant reads suppress the raw post, frame list and evidence details                                                                                     |
| `work_cloud_retained_frame`       | One authorized retained JPEG plus integrity metadata                                                  | Maximum 150,000 image bytes; native image content, not a claim that the full video was watched                                                             |

These are source-derived contract/read bounds, not measured total database bytes or a promise that every result fills its maximum.

## Read receipts as states

| Field or state                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Source ID / post URL                            | Which saved item an operation concerns                                                                                   |
| Queued, waiting, running                        | Accepted/in progress, not a completed analysis                                                                           |
| Generation / revision / grant version           | Concurrency and current-authority bindings for later requests                                                            |
| Analysis ID / context hash / selection revision | Exact saved analysis and project context used by a proposal or version selection                                         |
| Coverage / examined / next cursor               | What this bounded read covered and how to continue                                                                       |
| Maximum or reserved credits                     | An upper bound or temporary hold, not the final charge                                                                   |
| `chargedCredits: null`                          | No final charged amount is available. Check billingState; null alone means neither zero charge nor an active reservation |
| Catalog published                               | A neutral shared result exists; private notes/project plans do not become public                                         |
| Requested / reported model and effort           | Requested settings versus host-reported provenance; no automatic independent attestation                                 |
| Evidence hash                                   | Identity/integrity binding, not proof a claim is true                                                                    |
| Outcome report                                  | An assistant/user report, distinct from signed GitHub observations or verified test results                              |

## Example: queued is not finished

The following is a schematic explanation, not a byte-for-byte API response. Use the actual returned keys and IDs for subsequent calls.

```json
{
  "sourceId": "synthetic-post",
  "state": "queued",
  "maximumCredits": 3,
  "chargedCredits": null,
  "next": "Read the returned status or wait for the configured completion event"
}
```

## Errors and recovery

Common read/list/status tools advertise output schemas in discovery. The reference expands those schemas alongside exact inputs. Checked [synthetic examples](https://github.com/StefanDG1/vibescroll/blob/codex/launch-20261022-link-cloud-compatible-20261025/docs/developers/examples.json) use placeholder identifiers, never operator data. Older clients can keep the existing full/legacy formats.

MCP transport/authentication errors, strict-input errors and returned business errors are different boundaries. A tool can return `isError: true` even when its HTTP transport succeeded. An `mcp/www_authenticate` challenge indicates an authentication flow; a workspace-choice response does not.

`PROFILE_SELECTION_REQUIRED` supplies a `get_profile` next action. Keep the existing connection and choose the returned workspace. Version conflicts require a fresh read and reconciliation. Insufficient funding or credits requires that route's action; it cannot silently switch to a paid API or another executor.

Returned business failures include an allowlisted `code`, `stage`, `retryability`, opaque `correlation_id` and safe `next_action`. A correlation ID helps identify a response; it does not grant access or establish that a job failed before dispatch. `reconcile_first` means preserve the existing operation and read its status. Only an actual authentication failure carries the OAuth challenge. Provider availability errors must not send users through reconnection.

Some generic failures currently collapse to “Current authorization or evidence is unavailable.” This message alone does not identify an expired login, missing grant or unavailable evidence. The implementation needs more precise safe errors; repeatedly reconnecting is not a verified fix. Preserve queued/running/unknown jobs and their holds until their exact state is known.

## Read ranked context fields

`posts` holds one compact record per returned canonical post/version. Use `fetch_id` and the exact workspace/share references to read it. `matches` refers to those records with `post_id`. `access_paths`, when present, lists access observed on the emitted page rather than every possible share.

`scanned_candidates` counts newly examined candidates in this call. `session_candidates` counts them across signed continuation. Extended requests also report `loaded_candidates`, the compact prefix rows actually loaded, which can exceed newly examined candidates. `loaded_bytes` measures serialized instrumented document reads, not billed database bytes. Read these with `coverage`, `has_more`, `exhausted`, `truncated` and `next_cursor`; an empty partial page is not proof of absence.

Optional `project_fit` reports matched/total topic criteria for the current authorized project profile. A compact criteria list can omit detail with `criteria_omitted` while retaining the full counts. It ranks the emitted page, not the whole library or measured business outcomes. Retrieve exact project-application context when prior proposal/history details are needed.
skills.md:
A tool is a function the model can call. A skill is a workflow the host can load to guide when and how to use tools. A saved native monitor is a configured background task with its own trigger and instructions. These are separate parts of the integration.

## Nine packaged skills

The source plugin in `plugins/vibescroll` contains these skills:

| Skill                                                   | Workflow                                                                                 | Main tools                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [vibescroll-setup](#vibescroll-setup)                   | [Connect and read](/docs/mcp/first-workflow)                                             | `get_profile`, `open_vibescroll`                                           |
| [vibescroll-save](#vibescroll-save)                     | [Find and save](/docs/workflows/find-save), [analyze](/docs/workflows/analyze)           | `save_link`, quote/start and status                                        |
| [vibescroll-find](#vibescroll-find)                     | [Find cited knowledge](/docs/workflows/find-save)                                        | `search`, `fetch`                                                          |
| [vibescroll-library](#vibescroll-library)               | [Browse saved knowledge](/docs/workflows/find-save)                                      | `open_vibescroll`, embedded adapters                                       |
| [vibescroll-compare](#vibescroll-compare)               | [Compare retained results](/docs/workflows/reanalyze)                                    | `fetch`, analysis history/version/compare                                  |
| [vibescroll-status](#vibescroll-status)                 | [Follow observed progress](/docs/workflows/analyze)                                      | `get_job_status`, `video_analysis_status`                                  |
| [vibescroll-project-review](#vibescroll-project-review) | [Save proposals](/docs/workflows/proposals), [discuss plans](/docs/workflows/discussion) | Project context, proposal persistence, discussion and explicit quote/start |
| [vibescroll-work-review](#vibescroll-work-review)       | [Approve and follow work](/docs/workflows/handoff)                                       | Issue preview/approval/retry and outcome reports                           |
| [vibescroll-feedback](#vibescroll-feedback)             | [Record a judgment](/docs/workflows/handoff)                                             | `record_feedback`                                                          |

The plugin manifest identifies the setup skill for onboarding and the MCP endpoint. A manually added custom MCP connection can expose tools without installing those packaged skills. The source package is not proof that a particular ChatGPT account loaded them. The twelve repository coding skills under `.agents/skills` guide developers working on VibeScroll; they are not these end-user workflows.

OpenAI's [plugin packaging guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) documents how skills and MCP dependencies belong to an installed plugin. Tool descriptions still guide a host that only has the MCP connection.

### vibescroll-setup

Connect through supported OAuth and verify an existing workspace with a read. Setup does not require a sample analysis, draft or purchase.

### vibescroll-save

Save the supplied source with a stable key and follow its actual route. Save-only stays separate from analysis. Source text cannot authorize processing or a paid fallback.

### vibescroll-find

Search bounded authorized pages and fetch selected current evidence. Incomplete coverage is not absence. Preserve citations and version bindings.

### vibescroll-library

Open supported Library, Sources, Topics or Scroll views and deliberate read-only exports. Loaded counts do not imply full-library coverage.

### vibescroll-compare

Compare selected evidence while retaining disagreement and uncertainty. Comparison itself starts no processing, spending or publication.

### vibescroll-status

Read the exact saved source's observed state and reconcile uncertainty. Configure monitoring only through a supported host task with current authority.

### vibescroll-project-review

Use all post insights by default and keep project context separate from inspected code. Write a proposal in chat and persist it without API generation. Hosted generation remains an explicit quoted choice. Resume and reconcile the same saved version.

### vibescroll-work-review

Distinguish a private plan, approved issue, authorized coding, checked patch and reported outcome. Preview the exact issue before the user's approval. A saved handoff does not authorize implementation by itself.

### vibescroll-feedback

Record only an explicit current-evidence judgment. Keep useful, not relevant, already implemented, unsafe/unsupported and later distinct. An authenticated outcome report has separate provenance from verified tests or benefit.

## Events and automatic analysis

[MCP Events](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events) lets ChatGPT subscribe to server updates. A user chooses the monitor and what the configured task does when an event arrives. VibeScroll's saved-link route uses an exact saved analysis intent and current authority before it starts work.

The existing prepared route performs downloading/transcription/frame extraction on the service. A native task reads the retained evidence, inspects JPEGs and completes its exact leased analysis. It does not need a new downloader or transcription runtime for that prepared branch.

The native monitor prompt is not automatically installed into every chat. An event does not grant access by itself and is not a guarantee that a dormant unrelated conversation will reply. Refreshing tool metadata and renewing OAuth are also different actions from creating or changing a monitor.
host-support.md:
Verification date: November 1, 2026. Code support, an observed owner workflow and independent customer acceptance are different evidence. Feature flags, scopes, grants and host discovery determine the tools available to a particular connection.

## Capabilities and evidence

| Capability                        | Code-supported route                                                                       | Owner or production observation                                                                                      | Remaining acceptance                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Website library and saved plans   | Mobile-browser app with shared backend records                                             | Accepted Home, Library and proposal checkpoints                                                                      | Independent fresh paid-user journey remains open                                            |
| Ordinary custom MCP reads         | OAuth MCP tools with current access checks                                                 | Original owner connection reads saved/shared results; refreshed ChatGPT read the current discussion and linked issue | Every tool in every fresh host is not established                                           |
| Chat-written proposal persistence | Project context, save/read/list proposal tools                                             | Original embedded connection saved a proposal; backend create/edit/replay and shared website read passed             | Fresh custom-host write and issue invocation remain separate acceptance                     |
| Credit-funded video and plan jobs | Exact quote/start routes, personal credits and bounded provider funding                    | Retained owner managed/native video and plan-generation runs passed                                                  | General independent customer and failure-path acceptance remains open                       |
| Native prepared analysis          | Configured ChatGPT Events task, exact intent and lease, retained transcript and JPEG reads | Original owner monitor completed automatic prepared jobs and warm reuse                                              | Cold onboarding, broad platform reliability and arbitrary-host automation remain unverified |
| Embedded UI                       | Feature-gated cards and app-only adapters                                                  | Original ChatGPT connection opened the compact shared view                                                           | Each host's UI and viewport support must be checked                                         |
| Packaged skills                   | Nine skill files in the source plugin                                                      | Package contents are source-verified                                                                                 | Installation in the owner's manually configured custom host is not established              |
| Codex chat workflow               | Ordinary tools and supplied-text proposal persistence use the shared MCP contracts         | No universal Codex host acceptance is recorded by this documentation checkpoint                                      | Verify actual discovery, OAuth, images and task support separately                          |
| Text-only MCP client              | Ordinary results include text content                                                      | Local protocol fixtures cover the server contract                                                                    | Independent text-only client acceptance and compact-output changes require separate tests   |
| Local analysis execution          | Product direction retains a local option                                                   | Deferred                                                                                                             | No current general local-executor availability claim                                        |

The full reference lists 54 feature-enabled descriptors, including worker and embedded adapters. It is not a promise that all 54 appear in an ordinary chat. Events subscription methods are separate protocol operations.

## Authentication and task readiness

VibeScroll OAuth establishes library and action access. Host sign-in establishes the model allowance. Installed skills, discovered tools, Events subscription, monitor state and native worker capability are distinct.

A workspace selection does not require reconnecting. A missing or paused monitor is not evidence of expired OAuth. Supported tool refresh can update stale discovery metadata without recreating the connection. Revocation or an actual authentication challenge uses the host's protected connection flow.

## Funding and images

Host-written plans use the active host's allowance before VibeScroll persists them. API-start tools use their quoted route regardless of the calling chat. Server preparation can cost credits even when native reasoning uses a subscription. Compatible ready-cache reuse starts no new analysis.

Native retained-frame completion requires actual image inspection in a supported authorized task. Text about a screenshot cannot replace its pixels. A generic direct-completion contract for any active chat remains under investigation, not an available alternative.
subscription.md:
Yes, you can use the model allowance of your signed-in ChatGPT or Codex host for work performed inside that chat. The MCP connection supplies data and saves the answer. It does not transfer that subscription to VibeScroll's servers.

## Which route pays for which work

| Action                                                            | Where the AI work happens                                    | Usage or cost                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find or explain saved insights                                    | The active ChatGPT/Codex conversation                        | Host allowance; ordinary VibeScroll data access still applies                               |
| Write or revise a plan in chat, then call `save_project_proposal` | The active conversation; VibeScroll stores the supplied plan | Host allowance; saving starts no paid model generation                                      |
| Store a discussion message or completion report                   | VibeScroll validates and stores the supplied text            | No model generation from the persistence tool                                               |
| `start_project_plan` or a generating `reply_to_project_plan`      | VibeScroll's hosted API service                              | Quoted VibeScroll credits and provider funding                                              |
| `start_video_analysis` with `executor=gateway`                    | Server preparation, then an API model                        | Quoted preparation/analysis credits and provider funding                                    |
| Prepared video with `executor=work_cloud`                         | Server preparation, then the configured native host task     | Preparation may use VibeScroll credits; host analysis uses that user's plan and task limits |

Calling an API-start tool from a subscribed chat does not change its funding route. Conversely, saving a plan written by the chat does not require another API model to rewrite it. Source retrieval, transcription, storage and database delivery can still have infrastructure cost even when reasoning uses the host's allowance.

Personal credits and provider funding are separate. A quote maximum is a temporary upper bound; the final charge settles once under the quoted tariff. Cached ready reuse starts no new analysis charge. VibeScroll reserves finite provider capacity before dispatch, keeps ambiguous usage held and stops new work when that capacity is unavailable. Buying personal credits cannot repair unavailable provider capacity, and the service does not purchase funding automatically.

## Two authentications, with different purposes

You sign in to ChatGPT/Codex to use its model and product features. That session remains with OpenAI. Codex's supported ChatGPT sign-in provides subscription access; API-key sign-in uses API billing instead. See [OpenAI authentication](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth).

You separately connect VibeScroll through OAuth so the host can access your VibeScroll library and permitted project actions. Your existing VibeScroll connection is reused across supported calls. VibeScroll validates the resulting bearer token and its current grant; it does not use that token to invoke an OpenAI model.

VibeScroll does not need your ChatGPT password, subscription token or API key for ordinary in-chat reasoning. No additional “Sign in with ChatGPT inside VibeScroll” is needed for that workflow. The [MCP OAuth specification and OpenAI guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth) describe the connection boundary.

## Renewal and usage limits

OAuth access tokens can expire while refresh tokens let the host renew access without another interactive sign-in. Revocation, expired refresh credentials, changed scopes or provider/client configuration can still require reconnection. Neither MCP nor the current code establishes authentication forever.

The host counts its own model messages, context, reasoning and supported task usage under its plan and limits. A multi-step tool workflow can need multiple model turns. VibeScroll cannot report an exact percentage of your ChatGPT allowance consumed by a call or guarantee a particular host model/effort from a model's self-report.

## Current supported direction

Use MCP reads and chat-authored proposals when you are already working in ChatGPT/Codex. Use the explicit credit route for work you want VibeScroll's website to execute independently. Native subscription-funded video analysis still uses the configured host task; general commercial subscription inference directly on VibeScroll's servers remains gated and is not enabled by this OAuth connection.

For a prepared transcript and screenshots, an appropriately equipped active host could reason over that evidence without downloading or transcribing the video again. The existing production completion/lease route is bound to the native task. A generic “complete prepared analysis from any ordinary chat” contract remains a possible future simplification, not a claim about every current host.
mcp.md:
MCP is the connection between an assistant and VibeScroll's tools. It exposes functions with names, descriptions and input schemas. VibeScroll does not receive the whole chat or run the host's model.

## What makes the chat call a tool

1. Your host discovers tools from the connected MCP server using `tools/list`.
2. The model sees the available tool descriptions and input schemas alongside the conversation and any loaded instructions or skills.
3. When your request needs VibeScroll data or an action, the model selects a tool and supplies its arguments.
4. The host applies its own connection and approval rules, then sends `tools/call` to VibeScroll.
5. VibeScroll validates the arguments and authorization, performs the operation and returns a result. The model uses that result to continue the conversation.

Descriptions improve tool selection; they do not guarantee that a tool is selected for every request. Mentioning VibeScroll or explicitly asking to use its connected tools can remove ambiguity. This flow follows [OpenAI's MCP concepts](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/concepts/mcp-server).

## How a request reaches the database

The public endpoint is `https://scroll.companynerve.com/mcp`. Its Next.js route verifies the VibeScroll OAuth bearer token, including its signature, issuer, resource audience, client, user, consent session, scopes and timestamps. It forwards the same bearer token to the Convex HTTP action.

Convex independently validates the token. The HTTP handler applies a throttle and checks the token through AuthKit's user-info endpoint. The operation then checks the current VibeScroll user, workspace membership, grant, required action scope and applicable subscription or worker authority. A tool description cannot override those checks.

ChatGPT/Codex calls the server on your behalf. The model does not receive a database administrator credential, and a caller-supplied workspace ID cannot authorize another person's data. The [authentication guide](/docs/mcp/subscription) explains the separate host and VibeScroll sign-ins.

## What data the chat sends

The tool call contains the selected name and structured arguments: for example a search query, saved source ID, project ID, proposed text or an exact version reference. Requests also carry protocol and authentication metadata. VibeScroll does not automatically receive unrelated messages from the chat, repository files or your ChatGPT credentials.

A model can put user text into an argument when a tool accepts it. Do not interpret “no full chat access” as “no text ever leaves the chat.” The [generated schemas](/docs/mcp/tools) show the fields that can be sent.

## Shared analysis and personal context

A canonical post can have retained neutral analysis and evidence shared between authorized users. Asking to analyze that post can associate a compatible ready result with your library instead of repeating preparation and generation. Normal browsing does not subscribe every catalog post to your account.

Your notes, project context, proposals and discussions remain separate from the neutral shared result. Reading a shared result still checks your current access. A cache hit avoids new analysis; it does not remove authentication or database work.

## Automatic work is a separate path

An ordinary tool call happens in an active chat turn. A native Events subscription can notify a configured task about a saved link or completion. That task uses its saved instructions and authorized tools to continue work. It is not a promise that any unrelated chat receives an unsolicited completion message.

See [Skills and Events](/docs/mcp/skills) for the differences between tool metadata, packaged skills and the existing native monitor.
efficiency.md:
The shared database saves repeated preparation and model generation. It does not make every MCP request free of database or network work. Dated acceptance includes individual function read/return-byte samples. Those samples are not a complete per-MCP-request invoice or a latency percentile.

## What happens on each call

The HTTP tool path performs an authenticated throttle mutation and an AuthKit user-info request before dispatch. `get_profile`, `save_link`, `search` and widget profile discovery can also ensure current defaults. The actual operation then runs its queries, mutations or actions. Responses are private and use `no-store`.

`knowledgeReadContext` memoizes duplicate document/helper reads within one immutable query snapshot. It is not a cross-request MCP cache. Convex also manages its own query caching/invalidation, whose effectiveness must be measured for the actual request and changing authorization state.

## Keep cost dimensions separate

| Dimension              | What contributes                                                   | How to verify                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database work          | Documents/index entries read or written, access checks, validation | Actual Convex function/database metrics                        |
| Function/action work   | HTTP handler, queries/mutations, scheduling and external requests  | Function logs/metrics with safe correlation IDs                |
| Response transfer      | Serialized result, protocol envelope, duplicated representations   | UTF-8 byte count at the transport boundary                     |
| Image/storage transfer | Explicit JPEG fetch and retained asset delivery                    | Actual object-storage bytes and image count                    |
| Model context          | Tool descriptions, returned text/images and subsequent reasoning   | Host/provider usage when available; host accounting can differ |
| New analysis           | Download/FFmpeg/transcription/model job and retention              | Preparation and model receipts, credit settlement              |

Sending fewer JSON fields can reduce response/context size while still reading the same full stored document. A 10 KB response therefore does not establish 10 KB of database bandwidth. [Convex's read documentation](https://docs.convex.dev/database/reading-data) and [resource limits](https://docs.convex.dev/production/state/limits) describe why bounded indexed reads matter; this page does not substitute a guessed per-call price for real metrics.

## Current trade-offs

- `get_profile(detail="summary")` returns project identifiers and version metadata without profile bodies or evaluations. Omit `detail` for the compatible full response. Fetch the selected project's actual context only when needed.
- The compatible legacy search examines five permitted posts in application code. Opt-in `ranked_v1` uses compact native full-text candidates across the authorized workspace and retains bounded detail hydration. Both expose coverage and continuation.
- Ordinary results contain the same JSON in both text and structured content. `fetch(format="structured_v1")` supplies an `analysis` object and short readable text; the default legacy response keeps serialized analysis in `text`. Do not assume a host deduplicates text and structured data for token accounting.
- `list_project_proposals(detail="summary")` omits plan bodies and handoff snapshots. It preserves current project/source authorization and context checks. Full detail remains the default for older clients.
- An ordinary `read_post_frame` includes authority checks before and after a bounded storage GET with byte/hash/dimension verification, without a mutation. The worker-specific retained JPEG tool additionally acknowledges the read for completion eligibility. Neither path is just a string lookup.

## Workspace search and complete post references

The active workspace determines the searchable collection. Personal requested posts and team-shared posts reference shared canonical versions and evidence. Team members share their workspace's search entries; joining a team does not import personal posts. Current membership, assistant grant and any exact sharing grant remain authoritative.

`search(mode="ranked_v1")` reads compact indexed candidates and returns post metadata once with referring insight matches. It reports index readiness, examined candidates, session budget and continuation. The compatible legacy search still scans at most five authorized posts per page. A small page is not proof that the entire workspace lacks a relevant result. Initial index population is a separate bounded operation, not an implicit global database scan in search.

Ranked search examines at most 50 compact candidates per call, hydrates at most 8 sources and returns at most 20 matches under its response-byte limit. It stops before further source loading after its 8 MB serialized `db.get` budget; `loaded_bytes` measures those payloads, not actual Convex billing. Continuation is authenticated and stops at 200 examined candidates. This does not prevent a fresh query; ordinary account/client throttling remains separate. `index_ready` means initial population finished, while `exhausted` describes the current index, which may lag scheduled updates. Current authorization is rechecked even when indexed entries are stale. Ranked mode requires whole-workspace access. A source/space-limited grant uses compatible legacy search, whose candidates come from the permitted source/space indexes. It cannot enumerate the wider workspace index and then filter results after loading.

Optional category/platform/direct-save-date filters operate within the same candidate budget. Unknown shared-save dates are excluded from a date-constrained result rather than invented. Explicit `workspaceIds` can select up to three currently authorized workspaces. They share a per-call ceiling of 50 newly examined candidates, 8 hydrated sources and 20 results, with 200 newly examined candidates per session. Extended search reloads a bounded compact prefix, at most 200 rows per request, because Convex permits one pagination operation per function. `loaded_candidates` reports this separately. Fixed per-workspace quotas may leave capacity unused; narrowing the scopes is the supported way to concentrate it. Results deduplicate canonical identities while retaining access paths observed on that emitted page. This is not an exhaustive list of all possible sharing paths. All requested scopes are checked before searching; revoked access rejects continuation.

Project-aware search reads one permitted current project profile and reports deterministic topic coverage for emitted results. It ranks the returned page without discarding lower-scoring matches. This is not a global best-fit guarantee, a new AI call or inspected repository code. The host can try at most two extra short lexical queries when wording misses meaning, while keeping the same scopes and overall budget. Vector embeddings remain deferred until real query quality and index-cost evidence justify them.

Use `fetch(format="post_context_v1")` only when a specific post needs full context. Its pages contain retained transcript segments, observations and insights, plus one screenshot manifest. Original citation IDs resolve through these collections. Actual screenshots are individually demand-loaded, so a search does not attach all images or transcripts. These reads reuse retained data; they do not repeat preparation or analysis. Host text/vision usage and storage delivery still apply.

Workspace filters restrict disclosure, but Convex meters the full searched index size for full-text and vector search even when filters return few results. [Vector-search costs](https://docs.convex.dev/search/vector-search#costs), [full-text costs](https://docs.convex.dev/search/text-search#costs). Physical cost isolation and semantic search require measured workload decisions; no separate search provider or embedding route is implied by workspace filtering.

## Shared cache structure

Keep immutable neutral analysis and evidence under exact canonical post/version references. Keep each person's requested-post association, selected version and private notes separately. Keep project plans and discussions workspace-scoped. A ready-cache hit can reuse the shared result with zero new analysis credits while still paying the smaller access/read/transfer costs.

Permission changes must take effect on later reads. Do not put authenticated MCP results or private project context in a public CDN cache to improve hit rates. Use small metadata views and exact authorized detail reads instead.

## Measurement and compatibility

The optional `MCP_MEASUREMENT_SAMPLE_RATE` setting accepts a sample rate from 0 to 1 and defaults to 0. Its scalar observations contain operation, boundary, elapsed time, serialized response bytes, decoded image bytes and outcome. They contain no arguments, source text, tokens, account IDs or new database writes. Backend forwarding and tool-presentation spans overlap; do not add their durations. Tool-presentation bytes precede SDK framing and metadata.

Synthetic authorized fixtures produced these UTF-8 measurements. These are not production billing or host-token estimates.

| Fixture          | Backend response bytes | Application MCP result bytes | Instrumented db.get / query calls |
| ---------------- | ---------------------: | ---------------------------: | --------------------------------: |
| Profile full     |                   6248 |                        12737 |                              2 /6 |
| Profile summary  |                    831 |                         1897 |                              2 /5 |
| Fetch legacy     |                   1519 |                         3435 |                              4 /3 |
| Fetch structured |                   1505 |                         3317 |                              4 /3 |

The summary removes one evaluation query. Query-local memoization also avoids duplicate document reads during discovery and proposal listing without carrying access across requests. These operations can still read the same whole repository document, so smaller JSON does not prove less database bandwidth. The structured fetch primarily improves field access; this fixture shows only a small byte reduction. Keep text-only compatibility until actual host acceptance justifies further changes.

Search reports `scanned_posts`, `matched_items`, `has_more`, `exhausted` and `truncated`. Prefer `next_cursor` for both library and older source grants: it resumes overflow within the same candidate page before moving to later posts. It binds the query, current access and source/version fingerprint; changed evidence requires a fresh search. `next_offset` remains compatible legacy post-page navigation and cannot recover within-page overflow by itself. The 128-idea scan cap remains explicit. These fields describe the legacy bounded scan. Ranked mode uses separate compact full-text candidate accounting; neither route promises exhaustive semantic recall.

Use meaningful Events and bounded reconciliation rather than rapid polling. Live AuthKit, membership, grant and source checks remain in place. Authorization metadata is not cached across callers to claim faster access.

## Dated production samples

On November 1, one actual ChatGPT retrieval used these Convex function samples. They exclude the outer HTTP authentication/throttle/default queries and other child actions, so do not sum them as a full request invoice or use them as latency percentiles.

| Function                                | Database read bytes / documents | Return bytes | Execution seconds |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------: | -----------: | ----------------: |
| Complete retained post query            |                      28,068 /22 |       12,459 |            0.1445 |
| Ranked search query, 8 returned matches |                     183,813 /90 |        9,382 |            0.2864 |

Both queries report zero database writes. The existing screenshot action verifies actual bytes and returns a native image. All 8 manifest frames rendered across the initial and sequential diagnostic tests; 3 initial host -32603 failures had no corresponding backend image action in the captured window. The documented image workflow reads one frame at a time. This is an observed acceptance result, not a guaranteed latency or a diagnosis of those host failures.
contributing.md:
Keep the documentation tied to real tool discovery and synthetic examples. Public docs compile from an explicit allowlist and do not query a person's library or a model.

## Edit the source

1. Add or edit public Markdown under `docs/developers`.
2. Register its route, title, group and optional diagram in `manifest.json`. Keep existing URLs and tool anchors stable.
3. Update `packages/mcp/tool-guide.ts` when a real tool's primary group, skill tags or workflow changes. Keep schemas, scopes and annotations in the runtime registry.
4. Compare every field and effect claim with its handler and serializer. Label schematic examples and unpublished output schemas explicitly.
5. Update the dated changelog. Separate published behavior from a local candidate and unverified host acceptance.

Use existing requested-post access boundaries. Never add private operational notes, customer content, credentials, signed asset links or retained provider bodies to the public allowlist.

## Regenerate and check

Run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
node scripts/generate-mcp-reference.mjs
node scripts/generate-mcp-reference.mjs --check
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/mcp-reference.test.ts tests/tool-guide.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The generator discovers the feature-enabled registry using a synthetic `tools/list` request. Its invocation callback rejects tool execution. It also compiles only manifest-allowlisted Markdown into `content.generated.json`. Commit generated descriptors and public content with their sources.

The normal CI Vitest run includes the reference and guide checks. Reference drift, missing tool ownership and invalid skill tags fail these checks. Run the relevant lint, types, public-doc tests and required release checks for the change. Browser acceptance checks search, old deep links, mobile navigation, diagrams and disclosure behavior separately.

## Write safe examples

Start with a read-only request such as "Find my saved insights about retries; do not start analysis or spend credits." Use returned IDs for dependent operations. A synthetic ID illustrates a shape; it is not runnable account data.

Use synthetic serializer fixtures for exact output examples. Until an example is checked against a serializer, label it schematic and avoid presenting it as an exact contract. Include pending, stale and unknown outcomes where they affect recovery. Never test discovery by starting a paid job or publishing a sample issue.

## Review public claims

Keep infrastructure cost separate from model generation, quotes separate from holds, and holds separate from final charges. Record host-specific acceptance in [Host support](/docs/mcp/host-support). Additional suggestions in the owner review remain later work unless separately approved.
changelog.md:
This page distinguishes published documentation from local work. Verification date: November 1, 2026.

## November 1, 2026: retained posts and scoped discovery

Complete retained-post pages now separate transcript, insights and observations, with one screenshot manifest. The ordinary image tool returns verified native JPEGs without a worker lease or new analysis. Ranked search uses compact workspace entries and bounded continuation. Compatible summary and legacy reads remain available.

The extended workflow adds category/platform/date filters, selected-project topic coverage and explicit search across up to three authorized workspaces. It distinguishes newly examined candidates from compact prefix rows loaded, deduplicates post/version matches and preserves observed access paths. Source/space-limited grants use the existing scoped legacy route. One-time connection defaults include current joined teams while respecting existing access-off decisions and personal-post boundaries.

The public guide groups tools by workflow and links packaged skills. Real host acceptance is separate from installed skills or universal client support. The initial post/image/search checkpoint passed actual ChatGPT reads; initial image errors recovered with sequential reads. Query expansion is documented as a bounded lexical strategy. No embedding provider, automatic global catalog search or hosted subscription inference is enabled by these changes.

## November 1, 2026: published documentation baseline

Website commit `68ae312` published eight public documentation pages, three responsive diagrams, search and 53 generated feature-enabled descriptors. Exact CI and 16 staged plus 16 canonical documentation cases passed, alongside native search and Home/Library checks. Backend `1f96e6d` remained unchanged by that documentation release.

The original owner connection and later refreshed ChatGPT discussion read are accepted observations. They do not establish that every tool or packaged skill is installed in each host. See [Host support](/docs/mcp/host-support) for the current distinctions.
